output_json.diff_review: Only product change is in src/main/java/net/lingala/zip4j/unzip/UnzipEngine.java: a new private helper assertFileWithinDestination(file, new File(outPath)) is invoked at line 424, immediately after the target File is built (line 422) and before parent mkdirs (426), existing-file delete (431), and FileOutputStream creation (434) — so no filesystem side effects occur for a malicious entry. The helper compares File.getCanonicalPath() of the destination and target, allows only when the file equals the dest or starts with dest + File.separator, and correctly guards against prefix-sibling directories (e.g. /dest vs /destination). It throws ZipException on traversal and wraps IOException as ZipException. No new imports/dependencies. The sink at getOutputFileNameWithPath (line 475, unchanged) still concatenates naively, but the new guard neutralizes the traversal at the write point. Remaining diff hunks are POV files under .security-pipeline/pov/ (not product code) and generated target/ maven build artifacts (not source). POV itself is unmodified by the patch.
output_json.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the Docker wrapper: extractAll now throws ZipException ("illegal file name that breaks out of the target directory"), escaped target exists=false, confined target exists=false, prints "NOT VULNERABLE", POV_EXIT=1. Before patch the orchestrator log shows exit 0 (escaped file written). Vulnerability no longer reproduces.
output_json.regression_result: `mvn -B test` inside the container: BUILD SUCCESS (project has no test sources — "No tests to run"). `mvn -B -DskipTests package` in orchestrator log also BUILD SUCCESS. Compilation of the patched source succeeds. Legitimate entries resolve within the destination and pass the startsWith(dest+separator) check, so normal extraction is unaffected.
output_json.summary: The patch fixes the Zip Slip / path-traversal vulnerability (CWE-022) in UnzipEngine.getOutputStream() by validating the canonical resolved output path against the canonical destination directory before any mkdirs/delete/FileOutputStream side effect. Malicious entries like "../pov_pwned.txt" now throw a ZipException. Independently reran the POV (exits 1, NOT VULNERABLE, no escaped file) and the regression build/test (BUILD SUCCESS). Diff is minimal, appropriate, and does not touch the POV or disable functionality.
